keyDecisions: ADR-040 (Accepted): one decoded video -> many quads, each cropped, from a SINGLE decode. Frame-sync becomes structural (one clock/frame), decode cost flat in quad count. The mechanism is the TD-09 convergence: renderer resolves a quad's texture from SourceManager via the dormant TextureBinding::mediaId. Box-wrap MVP (panorama on a cuboid, 2 projectors / 2 scenes).

Crop is normalized (NormalizedRect cropRect, default full frame) and composes OUTSIDE the existing UV transform in quad.frag: uv = cropOffset + cropSize*uv. Identity is byte-for-byte the old formula (render no-op), so existing projects are visually unchanged.

Crop serialized inside textureBinding only when non-identity -> pre-crop .qmap files and untouched quads stay byte-identical; no version bump (matches the ADR-036/037 color/soft-edge conditional-write precedent). Missing crop loads as full frame.

Groups-on-load needed TWO fixes: (a) deserializeQuad/deserializeGroup now preserve the persisted id (defensive parseIdOrNull: malformed/short -> fresh, so older files still load) so member references re-link; (b) syncProjectToEditor rebuilds each scene's groups with member + nested-parent id remap (createQuad/createGroup mint fresh ids).
TD-07: fixed with DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT 60 (NOT DISCOVERY_MODE PRE_TEST — that was tried and reverted because it broke the standard `ctest --test-dir build/debug` which then required -C Debug).

P1 verification depth was the user's explicit choice: a real-GL GPU readback test (test_render_gl) — render through the actual shader to an FBO and glReadPixels — not just a data round-trip. It is the repo's first real-GL test; skip-if-no-context keeps it CI-safe.
P2 (the media-model convergence) is success-metric-adjacent and the highest-risk phase; deferred to a fresh start with an advisor pass rather than barrelled into at session end.

lessons: A 'crop the video into quarters' feature was already half-built in dormant scaffolding (TextureBinding::mediaId + cropRegion, SourceManager owning sources+textures) — audit for existing unused fields before designing; the real work was wiring, not inventing.

When restoring a feature that crosses serialize+load (groups), check the WHOLE chain: the linkage can be broken at the serializer (ids dropped) AND the bridge (not re-applied). Fixing only one leaves it broken.
Persisted-but-ignored id fields are a latent linkage bug (same shape as the TD-05 mesh-offset drop): writing an id you never read silently breaks any cross-reference that uses it.

CMake gtest DISCOVERY_MODE PRE_TEST defers discovery to ctest time but, on a multi-config (VS) generator, makes `ctest --test-dir` require -C <config>; a plain DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT bump fixes the build-exit flake without changing the developer's ctest invocation.

For a shader/visual feature, a data round-trip test is not 'seen working' — a real-GL FBO + glReadPixels test proves the pixels. It is cheap to stand up (hidden GLFW window + glad + the RAII Framebuffer) and worth it; skip-if-no-context keeps it CI-safe.
